_doc: Human verdicts on cells where the printed page disagrees with the catalog.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `apply_survey.py --conflicts` regenerates the queue from the sidecars
every run, so without a decision record it reprints the same items forever and nobody can
tell 'not yet reviewed' from 'reviewed, catalog was right'. The queue is derived; the verdict
is not. This is the verdict. `results/ditto_review_*.tsv` has the same missing half --
PIPELINE.md #1 asks to 'record which volume it was decided for' and nothing ever did.
VERDICTS
book-wins     the page is right and the CSV is wrong. THE ONLY verdict that overwrites a
non-empty cell, and it needs a reason naming the evidence.
catalog-wins  the CSV is right and the read is wrong. Retires the conflict.
both-right    both are true of different things -- a compiler vs the house that published.
Retires the conflict and marks the row as wanting a field split.
needs-image   text cannot settle it; hand to phase 3. Retires it from THIS queue only.
wontfix       not worth resolving; say why.
A decision is keyed (source, id, column) and is matched only against a conflict. It cannot
invent a cell, and a `book-wins` on a cell that no longer conflicts is a no-op.
THE SPOONER CLUSTER, SETTLED BY READING THE WHOLE SERIES (2026-09-22). Phase 3 read every
target card in micro_IABROOKLYN_0001-0028. The label was not simply wrong -- it was RIGHT, and
then carried past its expiry:
0001-0006  1822-1829  Alden Spooner, at the office of the Long-Island Star   CORRECT
0007-0009  1830-1832  Lewis Nichols, then William Bigelow    Spooner is the PRINTER
0010       1833/34    Nichols & Delaree                      wrong
0011       1834/35    Alden Spooner & William Bigelow        CORRECT AGAIN
0012-0014  1835-1838  Lewis Nichols                          Spooner prints it
0015-0018  1838-1842  Stevens & Marschalk, Ogden, Leslies    wrong
0019-0028  1843-1851  the Hearne brothers and partners       wrong
0022       1845/46    Silas H. Crowell                       wrong
0026       1848/49    E. B. Spooner, compiled by T. P. Teale CORRECT (a different Spooner)
THE SERIES CANNOT BE CORRECTED WHOLESALE. `spooner` is right on 8 of the 26 read and wrong on
18, and 0011 is BOTH -- Spooner co-compiles it and prints it. A rule that rewrote every
`spooner` row would have introduced six new errors to fix eighteen. That is why each row
carries its own read and its own verdict.
Alden Spooner published the 1820s volumes and PRINTED the 1830s ones. The catalog recorded the
name that stayed on the page while its role changed underneath -- and the extractor's
`published|printed` alternation then reproduced the same confusion a century later.
Still open: the 9 year reads that grabbed boilerplate or listing text. Recording
`catalog-wins` on those would paper over an extractor bug that should be fixed at the
source instead.

decisions.reason: Smith is the compiler the title is named for (SMITH'S BROOKLYN DIRECTORY); Charles Jenkins is the house that published it, per the copyright line on leaf 28. SURVEY_PLAN.md: these want separate `compiler` / `publisher` / `printer` fields.
Same Smith/Jenkins split as 1857BPL, attested by the target card on leaf 1 ('Published by Charles Jenkins').

Read is OCR-damaged ('GEORGE TTBiNfiTriM' for Upington). SURVEY_PLAN.md is explicit that character-level damage must stay a conflict rather than be matched loosely -- anything loose enough to match this would match unrelated houses.

No volume in this cluster names Spooner; Alden Spooner published Brooklyn directories in the 1820s and the label appears propagated across the microfilm series from the earliest volume.

Target card leaf 1: 'Brooklyn Directory, for 1832-33. Published by William Bigelow, 55 Fulton-street. Brooklyn: Printed by A. Spooner, 57 Fulton-street. 1832.' A TENTH spooner row, invisible until the extractor stopped preferring the printer -- and the one that explains the cluster: A. Spooner is the PRINTER here, and the sidecar now records him as such.

Target card leaf 1, read from the image: 'Brooklyn Directory for the year 1831. By Lewis Nichols, Brooklyn. A. Spooner, Printer, June 1831.' Spooner is named as the PRINTER on the page itself; the sidecar records him as such. Eleventh and twelfth rows of the spooner cluster, both invisible to phase 0 because the hOCR yielded no publisher at all.

Title page leaf 2, read from the image: 'BROOKLYN DIRECTORY, FOR THE YEARS 1837-38. BY LEWIS NICHOLS. BROOKLYN: A. SPOONER & SONS, PRINTERS.' Spooner is the PRINTER. The phase-0 candidate leaves (3/4/5) were all advertisement spreads, one of which carries an ad for 'A. SPOONER & SONS, Book & Letter Press Printers' -- a plausible source of the catalog's attribution. Eleventh and twelfth rows of the spooner cluster, both invisible to phase 0 because the hOCR yielded no publisher at all.

Target card leaf 1: 'Brooklyn Directory for the year 1830. By Lewis Nichols, Brooklyn: A. Spooner, Printer, June 1830.' Spooner is the PRINTER; Lewis Nichols compiled it. 1830 is where the catalog label stops being true.
Target card leaf 1: 'Brooklyn Directory, for 1836-37. Published by Lewis Nichols. Brooklyn: Printed by A. Spooner & Sons.' Spooner is the PRINTER.

Target card leaf 1 (underexposed frame, brightened): 'for 1841-2. Compiled by Thomas [Leslie] & John W. Leslie, and Published by them at the Reading and General Agency Office, 223 Fulton Street.' No Spooner involvement at all.
Target card leaf 1 (underexposed frame, brightened): 'Brooklyn City Directory for 1845 and 1846 ... Brooklyn: Silas H. Crowell, 1845. Douglas, Printer.' No Spooner involvement at all.

Read at leaf 323 = printed p.317 (GAS-GAY), the exact anchor the CSV note cites. Its offset (+6) checks out; its column count does not. The page is TWO columns. This also refutes the note's claim that 'the 2->3 transition is 1857->1859'. Each anchor leaf was opened and counted; the offsets recorded alongside these column counts are all correct, so it is specifically the column measurement that is wrong.

Read at leaf 338 = printed p.326 (GID-GIL), the anchor the note cites. Offset +12 checks out; the page is TWO columns, not 3. Each anchor leaf was opened and counted; the offsets recorded alongside these column counts are all correct, so it is specifically the column measurement that is wrong.

Read at leaf 511 = printed p.497 (GIE-GIL), the anchor the note cites. Offset +14 checks out; the page is TWO columns, not 3. Leaf 23 (printed p.31) is 2-column too, so it is not a mid-volume change. Each anchor leaf was opened and counted; the offsets recorded alongside these column counts are all correct, so it is specifically the column measurement that is wrong.

Read at leaf 7 = printed p.1025. FIVE columns. The CSV's 3 came from a bracket covering 1859-1915; 1922/23 is outside it, so this is a measured value rather than a correction. Each anchor leaf was opened and counted; the offsets recorded alongside these column counts are all correct, so it is specifically the column measurement that is wrong.

Title page leaf 17 carries TWO independent attestations of 1839: 'FOR THE SIXTY-FOURTH YEAR OF AMERICAN INDEPENDENCE' (1775+64) and the imprint's printed '1839'. The catalog's 1816 is wrong. This is one of the 16 IA-metadata errors the plan predicted, now confirmed from the page rather than inferred from a majority vote.

Title page leaf 7: 'PRINTED AND PUBLISHED AT THE OFFICE OF THE FLUSHING JOURNAL, FLUSHING, N. Y. 1890', copyright entered by C. W. Smith. The volume is not Boyd's. The 'JOHN J. BRENNAN, PROPRIETOR' phase 0b read from leaf 27 is a third name again, and sits elsewhere in the front matter.

Title page leaf 17: 'THE NEW-YORK CITY DIRECTORY, FOR 1854-1855. Thirteenth Publication. ESTABLISHED IN 1842.' The catalog's 1851 is wrong. Corroborated two ways: the copyright line on leaf 18 reads 'in the year 1854, by CHARLES R. RODE', and the printed volume number 13 against a printed origin of 1842 lands exactly on 1854.

Title page leaf 11 carries BOTH dates for different things: the work is 'THE NEW-YORK DIRECTORY ... BY DAVID FRANKS ... M, DCC, LXXX, VI' (1786 in roman numerals), and below a rule, 'REPUBLISHED BY JOHN DOGGETT Jr., 59 LIBERTY STREET, NEW YORK, 1851.' The catalog's 1786 is right about the work; phase 0b's 1851 is right about the artefact. Recorded as year=1786 plus reprint_year=1851 rather than forcing one to win.

Leaf 104 prints '106' in its head margin above the caption 'MERCEIN'S' and the listing's first entry 'Acbeson Hugh, cartman 39 Lombard'; leaf 105 prints 107. The preceding leaf 103 is an advertisement ('NEW-YORK ANNUAL ADVERTISER ... A. ARNOUX, MERCHANT TAILOR'), so the CSV's 105 is the ad page, one before the listing. https://iiif.archive.org/iiif/merceinscitydire00merc$104/full/!1400,1400/0/default.jpg
